description: Five multiple-choice questions plus two sliders (age, time horizon). Answers are scored on two separate axes, willingness (risk tolerance) and ability (risk capacity), then combined with an age anchor and a time-horizon cap into a stock / bond split.

questions.prompt: What do you want this money to do?

options.text: Stay safe. I mostly don't want to lose any of it
Keep up with inflation without much drama
Grow steadily toward a big goal like retirement
Grow as much as possible, even if the ride is bumpy

questions.prompt: You invest $10,000 for one year. Which range of outcomes would you sign up for?
A few months in, that $10,000 is worth $7,500. What do you actually do?

options.text: Sell everything before it gets worse
Sell some so I can sleep at night
Buy more while it's on sale

questions.prompt: If your income stopped tomorrow, how long could you pay your bills without touching this money?
Have you had money invested during a big market drop (like 2020 or 2022)?

options.text: Yes, and I sold some or all of it

sliders.prompt: How many years until you'll need most of this money?

results.label: Conservative Investor
results.shortDescription: Stability comes first. This mix keeps swings small, at the cost of slower long-term growth.

results.label: Cautious Investor
results.shortDescription: Some growth, but limiting losses still matters a lot. Defensive, with a foot in the market.

results.label: Balanced Investor
results.shortDescription: A middle ground: enough stocks to grow, enough bonds to soften the bad years.

results.label: Growth-Oriented Investor
results.shortDescription: Built for long-run growth. Expect real drawdowns, and the time to wait them out.

results.label: Aggressive Growth Investor
results.shortDescription: Almost all stocks. Big swings are the price of the highest expected long-term return.
